hints: Write transplant first and test it mentally on the root: if u->parent is NULL then v becomes the new tree root, which is why these functions return the root.
Cases 1 and 2 are one line each. Note that case 1 also covers a leaf (x->right is NULL, so you transplant NULL, which is exactly right).

Case 3: y = minimum(x->right). If y is NOT x's direct right child, first lift y out with transplant(T, y, y->right) and give y the old x->right. Then transplant x with y and hand y the left subtree. Skipping the 'y->parent != x' check corrupts the tree whenever the successor is adjacent.
source: NITC_Lab_S3_DSA Week 2 - BSTs, delete(T,x); the NITC 'BST Deletion' handout
title: BST deletion (transplant, all three cases)
